detail.body:
# feat(moe): logical token multiplicities and fixed-row router blocks

## What this PR does

In a packed layout one row can stand for several logical tokens. For example,
a shared prompt row stands for one copy of the prompt per completion. This PR
lets the MoE router count such rows correctly for expert-bias updates and makes
its forward routing scores independent of packing. Only
`local_tokens_per_expert` is weighted. Aux losses, z-loss, capacity dropping,
quantile balancing, routing replay and router diagnostics still count physical
rows, and the backward GEMMs are unchanged, so a caller must disable those
features. P6 rejects the loss, dropping, balancing and replay settings; router
diagnostics must be left off by the caller. Without a caller that opts in, routing is
unchanged.

## Changes

- `token_multiplicities` (optional, default `None`) on `TopKRouter.forward`,
  `InferenceTopKRouter.forward`, `TopKRouter.routing`,
  `TopKRouter._apply_expert_bias` and `MoELayer.route`. When set, each row is
  counted that many times in `local_tokens_per_expert`, so expert-bias updates
  match a dense forward. Counts stay exact in the existing int64 buffer.
  - On the default path, routers and routing callables are still called with
    exactly the upstream keywords.
  - Existing callers and replacement `routing` callables therefore keep
    working.
- `RouterInterface.forward` declares the optional argument, and the router
  docstrings describe it: one logical token count per flattened
  sequence-first row.
- `MoELayer._shared_prefix_token_multiplicities`: a per-call slot, `None` by
  default, that a caller sets around one layer call. Only the eager
  `MoELayer.forward` path reads it; paths that call `route()` directly or replay
  a CUDA graph ignore it.
- `moe_utils.router_gating_token_blocks()`: inside this scope the forward
  router GEMM runs over fixed row blocks. A packing change can otherwise select a
  different GEMM reduction, and even FP32 router differences below 2e-6 can
  flip BF16 expert choices.
- `tensor_parallel/random.py`: `CheckpointFunction` and
  `CheckpointWithoutOutput` recompute inside a copy of the forward pass's
  `contextvars` context.
  - CUDA autograd can run backward on an engine thread with different context
    values.
  - Without this change, a forward-scoped setting such as the router block
    scope is lost during recomputation.
  - Tensor observations stay suspended inside the restored context.
  - This applies to every recompute through these two helpers and keeps
    results unchanged. `te_checkpoint`, used with FP8/FP4, is unchanged.
- `RouterGatingLinearFunction.backward` computes only the gradients autograd
  requires. A frozen router still produces the input gradient but skips the
  weight-gradient GEMM, which has no consumer. This applies to every MoE run.

## Tests

```bash
python -m pytest tests/unit_tests/transformer/moe/test_router_shared_prefix.py \
    tests/unit_tests/tensor_parallel/test_random.py \
    tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/test_moe_kernels.py
torchrun --nproc-per-node=4 -m pytest tests/unit_tests/tensor_parallel/test_random.py \
    tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/test_moe_kernels.py
```

Results on one GB200 node (torch 2.11, Transformer Engine 2.15, mamba-ssm 2.3.2.post1, causal-conv1d 1.6.2.post1, flash-attn 2.8.1):

- one GPU: 122 passed, 16 skipped (multi-rank cases and optional TE/DeepEP features);
- four GPUs: 133 passed on every rank.

The only failures are existing `test_random.py` tests that need more ranks: `test_model_parallel_cuda_manual_seed` needs eight, and `test_checkpoint` needs TP2 (it passes on four GPUs). Both fail the same way on main. This branch alone on top of main also ran the surrounding regression suites (routers, attention, MTP, Mamba, training, RL) on one and four GPUs. Every failure in those runs also occurs on main in the same container: tests that need more ranks than the run had, and missing APEX extensions.

- `tests/unit_tests/transformer/moe/test_router_shared_prefix.py`:
  - the routing signature without multiplicities;
  - exact logical counts;
  - fixed-row blocks against per-block copies;
  - gradients for all seven combinations of trainable input, weight and bias.
    These run on the float64 `torch.mm` path; the Transformer Engine GEMM
    backward is not checked with frozen inputs.
- `tests/unit_tests/tensor_parallel/test_random.py`: the forward context is
  restored during recomputation, without duplicate tensor observations.
- `tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/test_moe_kernels.py`: bit-exact
  replays of the changed router paths.

## Shared-prefix stack

This PR is one of seven that #7914 was split into; #7914 itself is now P6, the
HybridModel integration. Each one needs fewer CODEOWNERS groups and can be
reviewed on its own. Shared-prefix
execution stores a prompt once per star (by default up to 16 completions of the
same group)
and runs those completions against it, instead of repeating the prompt in every
packed row.

| PR | Branch | Reviewer groups | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 #8152 RL packing library | `shared-prefix/p1-rl-packing` | reinforcement-learning | — |
| P2 #8153 MoE multiplicities and recompute context | `shared-prefix/p2-moe-multiplicities` | core, mixture-of-experts | — |
| P3 #8155 MTP loss groups | `shared-prefix/p3-mtp-loss-groups` | core, transformer | — |
| P4 #8156 forest attention and layout | `shared-prefix/p4-forest-attention` | core, transformer | — |
| P5 #8157 Mamba state fork | `shared-prefix/p5-mamba-state-fork` | core, hybrid-model | P4 |
| P6 #7914 HybridModel integration | `shared-prefix/hybrid-kernels-20261006` | core, hybrid-model | P1, P2, P3, P5 |
| P7 #8158 RL packaging | `shared-prefix/p7-rl-packaging` | ci, training | P1 |

P1 to P4 can merge in any order. A dependent branch carries its dependencies'
commits until they merge; review only its last commit.

Without a caller, P2 to P5 do not change existing numerics. Two P2 changes do
apply to every caller, and both keep results unchanged:

- recomputation through `tensor_parallel.checkpoint` and
  `CheckpointWithoutOutput` restores the forward pass's `contextvars` context
  (`te_checkpoint` is unchanged);
- the router GEMM backward skips gradients nobody requested.

P1 changes `megatron.rl` import-time behavior (lazy request types, lazy log
file). P6 is the first PR that wires the feature into a model.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

+def _expert_bias_token_counts(
+    routing_map: torch.Tensor,
+    padding_mask: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    token_multiplicities: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    *,
+    num_experts: Optional[int] = None,
+    out: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Count routed tokens per expert for boolean maps or dense top-k expert indices.
+
+    Counts are added in place to ``out`` (the expert-bias buffer) or to a new int64 tensor.
+    Padding and invalid (-1) dense routes contribute zero, with no data-dependent shapes.
+    Shared-prefix prompt rows pass ``token_multiplicities``: the number of logical copies
+    each row replaces. Without them, the kernels are the upstream expert-bias kernels.
+    """
+    use_dense_indices = routing_map.dtype != torch.bool
+    if padding_mask is not None:
+        padding_mask = padding_mask.reshape(-1)
+        if padding_mask.shape[0] != routing_map.shape[0]:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"MoE padding mask must contain one value per routed token: "
+                f"{tuple(padding_mask.shape)} vs routing map {tuple(routing_map.shape)}"
+            )
+    if out is None:
+        if not use_dense_indices:
+            num_experts = routing_map.shape[-1]
+        elif num_experts is None or num_experts < 1:
+            raise ValueError("Dense expert indices require an explicit positive num_experts")
+        out = torch.zeros(num_experts, dtype=torch.int64, device=routing_map.device)
+    if token_multiplicities is not None:
+        token_multiplicities = token_multiplicities.reshape(-1)
+        if token_multiplicities.shape[0] != routing_map.shape[0]:
+            raise ValueError("MoE token multiplicities must contain one value per routed token")
+        if token_multiplicities.device != routing_map.device:
+            raise ValueError("MoE token multiplicities must be on the routing-map device")
+        # Accumulate in the count dtype (int64 for the expert-bias buffer) so large logical
+        # counts stay exact; multiplicities are small integers in any input dtype.
+        token_multiplicities = token_multiplicities.to(out.dtype)
+
+    if not use_dense_indices:
+        if padding_mask is not None:
+            routing_map = routing_map & (~padding_mask).unsqueeze(-1)
+        if token_multiplicities is not None:
+            routing_map = routing_map * token_multiplicities.unsqueeze(-1)
+        out += routing_map.sum(dim=0)
+        return out
+
+    # Fixed-shape counting: keep every [num_tokens, topk] slot and give padding tokens and
+    # invalid (-1) routes a zero weight instead of filtering rows, which would be a
+    # data-dependent shape (nonzero + host sync) inside the compiled expert-bias update and
+    # inside the moe_router CUDA graph scope.
+    expert_indices = routing_map.reshape(-1).to(torch.long)
+    if token_multiplicities is None:
+        token_counts = torch.ones_like(expert_indices, dtype=out.dtype)
+    else:
+        token_counts = token_multiplicities.unsqueeze(-1).expand_as(routing_map).reshape(-1)
+    if padding_mask is not None:
+        valid = (~padding_mask).unsqueeze(-1).expand(-1, routing_map.shape[-1])
+        token_counts = token_counts * valid.reshape(-1).to(token_counts.dtype)
+    invalid_routes = expert_indices < 0
+    expert_indices = expert_indices.masked_fill(invalid_routes, 0)
+    token_counts = token_counts.masked_fill(invalid_routes, 0)
+    if torch.are_deterministic_algorithms_enabled():
+        out.index_add_(0, expert_indices, token_counts)
+    else:
+        out.scatter_add_(0, expert_indices, token_counts)
+    return out
+

+    routes = torch.tensor([[0, 2], [1, 3], [2, 3], [0, -1]])
+    bool_routes = torch.zeros(4, 4, dtype=torch.bool)
+    for row, experts in enumerate(routes.tolist()):
+        for expert in experts:
+            if expert >= 0:

+    padding_mask = torch.tensor([False, True, False, False]) if padding else None
+    multiplicities = torch.tensor([3, 1, 2, 5])
+    route_map = routes if dense_indices else bool_routes

+    returned = _expert_bias_token_counts(route_map, padding_mask, out=counts)
+    assert returned is counts

+
+    counts = torch.full((4,), 7, dtype=torch.int64)
+    _expert_bias_token_counts(route_map, padding_mask, multiplicities, out=counts)
+    weights = (multiplicities * keep).unsqueeze(-1)

+            hidden_size=12,
+            num_attention_heads=4,
+            num_moe_experts=8,
+            use_cpu_initialization=True,
+            moe_router_load_balancing_type="none",
+            moe_router_score_function="sigmoid",
+            moe_router_enable_expert_bias=True,
+            moe_router_topk=2,
+            add_bias_linear=False,
+        )
+        submodules = get_submodules(
+            get_gpt_layer_local_submodules(num_experts=8, moe_grouped_gemm=False).mlp
+        )
+        router = MoELayer(config, submodules).router.cuda()
+        hidden_states = torch.randn(6, 2, 12, device="cuda")
+        padding_mask = None
+        if with_padding:
+            padding_mask = torch.zeros(6, 2, dtype=torch.bool, device="cuda")
+            padding_mask[4:, 1] = True
+        # Float32 multiplicities, as a shared-prefix layout produces them.
+        multiplicities = torch.tensor(
+            [4, 1, 1, 3, 1, 1, 2, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1], dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda"
+        )
+        router.local_tokens_per_expert.zero_()
+        with torch.enable_grad():
+            _, routing_map = router(
+                hidden_states, padding_mask, token_multiplicities=multiplicities
+            )
+        keep = torch.ones(12, dtype=torch.bool, device="cuda")
+        if padding_mask is not None:
+            keep = ~padding_mask.reshape(-1)
+        weights = (multiplicities.long() * keep).unsqueeze(-1)
+        expected = (routing_map.bool() * weights).sum(dim=0)
+        assert router.local_tokens_per_expert.dtype == torch.int64
+        assert torch.equal(router.local_tokens_per_expert, expected)
+    finally:
+        Utils.destroy_model_parallel()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "requires", [combo for combo in itertools.product([False, True], repeat=3) if any(combo)]
+)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("block_size", [None, 3])
+def test_router_frozen_parameters_preserve_requested_gradients(requires, block_size):
+    """The router GEMM backward computes only the gradients its inputs require."""
+    generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(901)
+    values = [
+        torch.randn(shape, generator=generator, dtype=torch.float64)
+        for shape in [(7, 1, 5), (4, 5), (4,)]
+    ]
+    actual_inputs = [value.clone().requires_grad_(need) for value, need in zip(values, requires)]
+    reference_inputs = [value.clone().requires_grad_(need) for value, need in zip(values, requires)]
+    if block_size is None:
+        actual = router_gating_linear(*actual_inputs, torch.float64)
+    else:
+        with router_gating_token_blocks(block_size):
+            actual = router_gating_linear(*actual_inputs, torch.float64)
+    reference = torch.nn.functional.linear(*reference_inputs)
+    cotangent = torch.randn(actual.shape, generator=generator, dtype=torch.float64)
+    actual.backward(cotangent)
+    reference.backward(cotangent)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, reference, rtol=1e-12, atol=1e-12)
+    for value, reference_value, need in zip(actual_inputs, reference_inputs, requires):
+        if need:
+            torch.testing.assert_close(value.grad, reference_value.grad, rtol=1e-12, atol=1e-12)
+        else:
+            assert value.grad is None
+
+
+def _blocked_reference(inp, weight, bias, block_size):
+    # Reference: pad and run every block as a separate copy.
+    outputs = []
+    for start in range(0, inp.shape[0], block_size):
+        rows = inp[start : start + block_size]
+        padded = torch.nn.functional.pad(rows, (0, 0, 0, block_size - rows.shape[0]))
+        outputs.append(moe_utils._router_gating_gemm(padded, weight, bias, torch.float32))
+    return torch.cat(outputs)[: inp.shape[0]]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_rows", [1, 7, 8, 9, 24, 29])
+def test_router_gemm_blocks_use_views_of_one_padded_input(num_rows):
+    block_size = 8
+    inp = torch.randn(num_rows, 1, 5, dtype=torch.float64)
+    weight = torch.randn(3, 5, dtype=torch.float64)
+    seen = []
+    gemm = moe_utils._router_gating_gemm
+
+    def recording_gemm(rows, *args):
+        seen.append((rows.shape, rows.untyped_storage().data_ptr()))
+        return gemm(rows, *args)
+
+    with patch.object(moe_utils, "_router_gating_gemm", recording_gemm):
+        with router_gating_token_blocks(block_size):
+            actual = router_gating_linear(inp, weight, None, torch.float64)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, inp @ weight.t(), rtol=0, atol=1e-12)
+    assert actual.shape == (num_rows, 1, 3)
+    assert len(seen) == -(-num_rows // block_size)
+    assert all(shape == (block_size, 5) for shape, _ in seen)
+    assert len({storage for _, storage in seen}) == 1
+
+
+def test_router_gemm_default_path_skips_blocks():
+    inp = torch.randn(9, 1, 5, dtype=torch.float64)
+    weight = torch.randn(3, 5, dtype=torch.float64)
+    with patch.object(moe_utils, "_router_gating_gemm_blocks", side_effect=AssertionError):
+        actual = router_gating_linear(inp, weight, None, torch.float64)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, inp @ weight.t(), rtol=0, atol=1e-12)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="needs the TE/cuBLAS router GEMM")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("input_dtype", [torch.float32, torch.bfloat16])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("with_bias", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_rows", [1, 333, 1024, 2048, 2500])
+def test_router_gemm_blocks_bitwise_match_per_block_copies(input_dtype, with_bias, num_rows):
+    generator = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(num_rows)
+    inp = torch.randn(num_rows, 1, 256, device="cuda", generator=generator).to(input_dtype)
+    weight = torch.randn(64, 256, device="cuda", generator=generator).to(input_dtype)
+    bias = torch.randn(64, device="cuda", generator=generator).to(input_dtype)
+    bias = bias if with_bias else None
+    with router_gating_token_blocks(1024):
+        actual = router_gating_linear(inp, weight, bias, torch.float32)
+    expected = _blocked_reference(inp.view(num_rows, -1), weight, bias, 1024)
+    assert torch.equal(actual.view(num_rows, -1), expected)
